extraction.name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
extraction.description: OpenThoughts3-1.2M is a state-of-the-art open-source dataset for training reasoning models, containing 1.2 million examples across math (850K), code (250K), and science (100K) domains. The dataset was constructed through systematic investigation of data generation pipeline choices via 1,000+ controlled experiments. Questions are sourced from high-quality origins (OpenMath-2-Math, CodeGolf, OpenCodeReasoning, StackExchange Physics, Organic Chemistry PDFs), filtered using LLM-based difficulty and response-length criteria, and answered with QwQ-32B as the teacher model with 16x sampling per question. The resulting OpenThinker3-7B model, finetuned from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, achieves state-of-the-art results on reasoning benchmarks including AIME 2025 (53%), LiveCodeBench 06/24-01/25 (51%), and GPQA Diamond (54%).
extraction.creator: OpenThoughts Team (Stanford University, University of Washington, BespokeLabs.ai, Toyota Research Institute, UC Berkeley, UT Austin, UCLA, JSC, LAION, NYU, UNC Chapel Hill, ASU, Lila Sciences, Cornell Tech, TUM, Open-Sci Collective)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed through a systematic experimental pipeline consisting of six stages: (1) sourcing questions from existing datasets and newly generated ones across math, code, and science domains; (2) mixing questions from top-performing sources; (3) filtering for high-quality questions using fastText or LLMs; (4) deduplicating questions and sampling multiple answers per question; (5) filtering out low-quality answers; and (6) selecting the best teacher model (QwQ-32B). Over 1,000 controlled experiments were conducted to optimize each pipeline step.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Web Scraping, Document analysis, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were sourced from 27 code sources, 21 math sources, and 14 science sources, including StackExchange CodeGolf, OpenCodeReasoning, OpenMath-2-Math, NuminaMath-1.5, StackExchange Physics, and organic chemistry textbooks/PDFs. Final dataset uses OpenMath-2-Math for math, CodeGolf and OpenCodeReasoning for code, and StackExchangePhysics and OrganicChemistryPDFs for science.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Answers were generated using QwQ-32B as the teacher model with 16x sampling per question. For math and science, exact deduplication was applied. For code, no deduplication was applied. Questions were augmented/generated using GPT-4o-mini for some sources.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were filtered using LLM-based methods: difficulty-based filtering with GPT-4o-mini for code questions, and response length filtering with GPT-4.1-mini for math and science questions. Decontamination was performed against evaluation benchmarks using both Indel similarity (threshold 75%) and N-gram-based similarity (N=13) to remove contaminated samples. Final dataset contains 850K math, 250K code, and 100K science datapoints.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Answers (reasoning traces and final answers) were generated by the QwQ-32B teacher model. Multiple answers (16x) were sampled per question to increase dataset diversity. No answer filtering was applied in the final pipeline as experiments showed no filtering strategy outperformed using all answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Curator framework (custom data generation framework); DeepSeek API, OpenAI API for auxiliary annotation tasks
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Multiple answer filtering strategies were explored including majority consensus, GPT verification, length-based filtering, and FastText classifiers. None significantly outperformed the no-filtering baseline, so no answer filtering was applied.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: No human annotators; annotations are machine-generated by QwQ-32B
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: QwQ-32B (primary teacher model), DeepSeek-R1 (compared teacher), Phi-4-reasoning-plus (compared teacher), GPT-4o-mini (for question filtering and difficulty rating), GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1-nano, Gemini-2.0-flash-lite (for PDF OCR extraction), FastText classifiers
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Datasets and models are released on openthoughts.ai, Hugging Face (https://huggingface.co/open-thoughts), and GitHub (https://github.com/open-thoughts/open-thoughts). The project has progressed through four generations: BespokeStratos-17K, OpenThoughts-114K, OpenThoughts2-1M, and OpenThoughts3-1.2M.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors note a safety trade-off: supervised fine-tuning on reasoning data inadvertently degrades pre-existing safety alignment of base models. OpenThinker3-7B shows increased harmfulness rate (55.5 on Harmbench) compared to base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (14.5), as the dataset was trained without explicit safety-tuning or alignment-focused data. Future work should incorporate safety-specific datasets.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The work did not explore datasets for reinforcement learning. Within SFT, staged SFT or curriculum learning was not explored. The pipeline selected strategies maximizing overall average benchmark performance rather than optimizing per domain. Distilled reasoning models still exhibit generalization deficits, showing strong performance fluctuations on simple problem variations (Alice in Wonderland evaluation). Safety alignment is degraded compared to the base model. Some benchmarks show saturation (AMC23, MATH500) while others (HLE) do not respond to scale.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training (Supervised Fine-Tuning) of reasoning models for math, code, and science reasoning tasks. The dataset is designed for SFT post-training of language models to develop long chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities. Used to train OpenThinker3-7B from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct base model.
